Task: Grounding LLM high-level planning of long-horizon natural-language instructions in robot affordances.
Method: Score candidate skills by LLM relevance times value-function affordance of pretrained language-conditioned skills; greedy skill selection.
Setup and data: Real mobile manipulator, real-world environments; library of pretrained language-conditioned skills; PaLM and other LLMs.
Key result: Abstract reports successful completion of long-horizon abstract instructions and that grounding is needed; no numbers in abstract.
Limitation: Requires pre-trained skills with value functions; relies on large proprietary LLMs; skill set fixed.
Edge footprint (as published): LLM inference (PaLM-scale) needs datacentre GPUs/TPUs; skill value functions are lighter. Not Pi-class as published.
Role in the framework: Baseline to beat / component to reuse: prototypical LLM + learned-affordance fusion for skill selection.

Task: Closed-loop LLM planning for robot instruction following using environment feedback.
Method: Inject textual feedback (success detection, scene description, human answers) into the LLM prompt for replanning; no fine-tuning.
Setup and data: Three domains: simulated and real tabletop rearrangement; real kitchen long-horizon mobile manipulation.
Key result: Abstract reports substantially improved instruction completion with closed-loop feedback; no numbers in abstract.
Limitation: Depends on feedback-module accuracy; growing prompt context; large LLM required; uncalibrated textual signals.
Edge footprint (as published): Uses large cloud-hosted LLMs; feedback modules (detectors, captioners) GPU-bound. Not Pi-class as published.
Role in the framework: Competing approach / component: verbal feedback fusion for recovery; motivates numeric confidence fusion instead.

Task: Zero-shot decomposition of high-level household tasks into admissible action plans with LLMs.
Method: Prompted LLM planning conditioned on example demonstrations plus semantic translation of steps to admissible actions.
Setup and data: VirtualHome simulator; executability metrics and human evaluation of correctness.
Key result: Abstract: substantially improved executability over LLM baseline; executability–correctness trade-off observed; no numbers given.
Limitation: Simulation only; symbolic actions; no perception or feedback; correctness drops as executability rises.
Edge footprint (as published): Large LLMs (GPT-3/Codex scale) via cloud; translation model is small. Planner not Pi-class as published.
Role in the framework: Component to reuse: constraining LLM output to an admissible action (modality) set.

Task: Natural-language outdoor navigation for a mobile robot without language-annotated data.
Method: Compose GPT-3 (landmark parsing), CLIP (landmark grounding) and ViNG (topological graph navigation).
Setup and data: Real mobile robot, complex outdoor environments, long-horizon routes.
Key result: Demonstrated long-horizon language-guided navigation; no numbers in abstract.
Limitation: Needs pre-built topological graph; landmark-only instructions; relies on cloud LLM.
Edge footprint (as published): GPT-3 via cloud; CLIP and ViNG run on an onboard GPU-class computer; CLIP small variants may fit Pi-class with latency cost.
Role in the framework: Component to reuse / evaluation reference: modular frozen-model composition; CLIP scores as perception confidence.

Task: Generating robot policy code from natural-language commands.
Method: Few-shot prompted code LLMs composing perception/control APIs; hierarchical recursive code generation.
Setup and data: Multiple real robot platforms; tabletop manipulation and other tasks; HumanEval for code generation.
Key result: 39.8% of HumanEval problems solved with hierarchical code generation.
Limitation: Relies on hand-designed APIs and perception; no uncertainty or failure-recovery mechanism.
Edge footprint (as published): Code LLM (Codex-class) queried via cloud; generated code itself runs cheaply on a Pi.
Role in the framework: Competing approach: LLM-as-programmer orchestration; generated code is edge-friendly.

Task: Grounding a language model in continuous robot sensor inputs for embodied reasoning.
Method: Inject encoded images/states as tokens into PaLM; joint multi-task training on robotics and vision-language data.
Setup and data: Several robot embodiments; manipulation planning, VQA, captioning.
Key result: PaLM-E-562B reported state of the art on OK-VQA; positive transfer from joint training.
Limitation: Enormous model size; high-level planning only; not open.
Edge footprint (as published): 562B parameters; TPU-pod scale. Far beyond Pi-class; cloud only.
Role in the framework: Competing approach: monolithic embodied LLM versus lightweight modular orchestrator.

Task: Interleaving reasoning and acting in LLM agents for QA and interactive decision-making.
Method: Few-shot prompting producing interleaved thought, action and observation steps.
Setup and data: HotpotQA, FEVER (with Wikipedia API); ALFWorld and WebShop text environments.
Key result: +34% (ALFWorld) and +10% (WebShop) absolute success over imitation/RL baselines with 1–2 in-context examples.
Limitation: Prompt-engineering sensitivity; large-model dependence; context growth; no uncertainty estimate.
Edge footprint (as published): Prompting only; works with any LLM, but reported results use large cloud models (PaLM/GPT-3). Small local LLMs feasible with lower accuracy.
Role in the framework: Baseline to beat / component to reuse: reason–act loop template for the orchestrator.

Task: Teaching language models to decide when and how to call external tools.
Method: Self-supervised annotation of API calls filtered by LM-loss reduction, followed by fine-tuning.
Setup and data: Text corpus; tools: calculator, QA system, two search engines, translator, calendar; zero-shot downstream tasks.
Key result: Abstract: substantially improved zero-shot performance, often competitive with much larger models; no numbers given.
Limitation: No chained or interactive tool use; filter based on LM loss; text-only.
Edge footprint (as published): Base model mid-sized (GPT-J-class); fine-tuning needs GPUs; inference of a few-billion-parameter model marginal on Pi-class with quantisation.
Role in the framework: Component to reuse: self-supervised learning of when to invoke an external module.

Task: Improving language agents from trial-and-error without weight updates.
Method: Verbal self-reflection on feedback stored in episodic memory to condition future trials.
Setup and data: Sequential decision-making, coding (HumanEval) and language reasoning benchmarks.
Key result: 91% pass@1 on HumanEval vs 80% for GPT-4.
Limitation: Requires strong base LLM for good reflections; memory bounded by context; no guarantees.
Edge footprint (as published): No training; inference cost of repeated trials; feasibility on Pi depends on the base LLM size.
Role in the framework: Component to reuse: training-free episodic self-improvement alongside LoRA/replay.

Task: Situated robot task planning with LLMs that respects available actions and objects.
Method: Programmatic prompts listing actions/objects with example programs; assertion-based feedback.
Setup and data: VirtualHome household tasks; physical robot arm for tabletop tasks.
Key result: State-of-the-art success rates in VirtualHome (per abstract); no numbers in abstract.
Limitation: Hand-specified action/object vocabulary; limited closed-loop recovery.
Edge footprint (as published): Large cloud LLM for planning; executing generated programs is cheap on edge hardware.
Role in the framework: Component to reuse: program-structured prompting to constrain orchestrator outputs.

Task: Zero-shot synthesis of manipulation trajectories from open-set language instructions.
Method: LLM-generated code queries a VLM to compose 3D affordance/constraint value maps; model-based planning over the maps; optional learned dynamics.
Setup and data: Simulated and real-robot environments; large variety of everyday manipulation tasks.
Key result: Large-scale study reported; no numbers in abstract.
Limitation: Depends on open-vocabulary detection/segmentation quality; cloud LLM/VLM; planning latency.
Edge footprint (as published): LLM and VLM calls need cloud/GPU; voxel planner moderately heavy. Not Pi-class as published.
Role in the framework: Competing approach / confidence-signal source: perception-grounded value maps for manipulation.

Task: Translating natural-language instructions into low-level robot behaviour via rewards.
Method: LLM generates reward parameters; real-time MuJoCo MPC optimises behaviour; interactive user corrections.
Setup and data: 17 tasks on a simulated quadruped and dexterous manipulator; real robot arm validation.
Key result: 90% of tasks solved vs 50% for Code-as-Policies primitive-skill baseline.
Limitation: Requires accurate dynamics model for MPC; reward templates hand-designed; cloud LLM.
Edge footprint (as published): MPC in MuJoCo needs a capable CPU; LLM via cloud. Real-time MPC unlikely on Pi 5 for complex bodies.
Role in the framework: Competing approach: LLM-to-reward interface feeding an RL/MPC modality.

Task: Few-shot high-level planning for vision-and-language embodied agents.
Method: In-context LLM planning with grounded dynamic re-planning using observed objects.
Setup and data: ALFRED benchmark (simulated household tasks).
Key result: Competitive with full-data baselines using <0.5% of paired training data.
Limitation: Simulation only; relies on external low-level controller and detector; cloud LLM.
Edge footprint (as published): LLM planner via cloud (GPT-3); planner calls are infrequent, so latency tolerable; not Pi-local as published.
Role in the framework: Evaluation reference / component: failure-triggered re-planning.

Task: Deliberate multi-path reasoning and search with LLMs.
Method: Tree search over LLM-generated thoughts with LLM self-evaluation, lookahead and backtracking.
Setup and data: Game of 24, Creative Writing, Mini Crosswords with GPT-4.
Key result: Game of 24: 74% success vs 4% for GPT-4 chain-of-thought.
Limitation: Many LLM calls per problem; heuristic self-evaluation not calibrated.
Edge footprint (as published): Multiplies inference cost; reported with GPT-4 via cloud. Poor fit for Pi-class budgets.
Role in the framework: Competing approach / evaluation reference: deliberative reasoning at high compute cost.

Task: Uncertainty alignment for LLM robot planners: knowing when to ask for help.
Method: Multiple-choice next-step generation; conformal prediction over LLM option likelihoods to form prediction sets; ask for help when set is non-singleton.
Setup and data: Simulated and real robot setups; ambiguity types including spatial, numeric, preferences, Winograd schemas.
Key result: Statistical task-completion guarantees with reduced help; favourable versus ensembles and prompt-tuning baselines (no numbers in abstract).
Limitation: Requires calibration data exchangeable with deployment; needs token likelihoods; single-step coverage compounding in multi-step tasks.
Edge footprint (as published): Calibration is cheap post-hoc; cost dominated by LLM (PaLM-scale in paper). Method itself applies to small local LLMs.
Role in the framework: Confidence-signal source / component to reuse: conformal calibration of orchestrator choices and escalation rule.

Task: Fine-tuning language models to act as agents rather than relying on prompting.
Method: Supervised fine-tuning on GPT-4-generated agent trajectories from multiple tasks and prompting methods (FireAct).
Setup and data: QA with Google search API (HotpotQA and other QA tasks); Llama-2 and other base models.
Key result: Llama2-7B fine-tuned on 500 GPT-4 trajectories: 77% HotpotQA performance increase.
Limitation: Single tool, text-only QA; teacher-dependent; no embodied tasks.
Edge footprint (as published): 7B models; fine-tuning on a GPU; quantised 7B inference borderline on a Pi 5 (slow). Smaller models would be needed.
Role in the framework: Component to reuse: distillation-style fine-tuning recipe for a small local orchestrator.

Task: Open-ended lifelong skill acquisition by an LLM agent in Minecraft.
Method: Automatic curriculum, code skill library, iterative prompting with feedback, errors and self-verification.
Setup and data: Minecraft (MineDojo/Mineflayer API).
Key result: 3.3× more unique items, 2.3× longer distances, up to 15.3× faster tech-tree milestones vs prior SOTA.
Limitation: GPT-4 black-box dependence; game setting with high-level APIs; cost of many queries.
Edge footprint (as published): Depends on GPT-4 cloud queries; not feasible on-device as published.
Role in the framework: Component to reuse: skill library and self-verification for online improvement.

Task: Aligning LLM planner uncertainty with instruction ambiguity for safe, compliant robot planning.
Method: Retrieval of introspective reasoning examples (post-hoc rationales of human-selected plans) combined with conformal prediction.
Setup and data: Three evaluation tasks including a new safe mobile manipulation benchmark.
Key result: Improved compliance and safety over SOTA LLM planners; tighter conformal bounds with fewer clarifications (no numbers in abstract).
Limitation: Knowledge base requires human-labelled plans; retrieval dependence; exchangeability assumption.
Edge footprint (as published): Retrieval and calibration cheap; LLM cost dominates. Could pair with a small local LLM, untested.
Role in the framework: Confidence-signal source / component to reuse: retrieval-augmented calibration of choices.

Task: Language-instructed multi-robot task planning with success-rate guarantees.
Method: Distributed LLM planner (S-ATLAS) with conformal prediction for per-robot uncertainty and help requests.
Setup and data: Multi-robot teams on language-specified tasks; comparative experiments with related planners.
Key result: Achieves user-specified success rates with fewer help requests; more efficient than baselines (no numbers in abstract).
Limitation: Guarantees assume successful plan execution; calibration data needed.
Edge footprint (as published): Conformal step cheap; LLM inference cost per robot; not demonstrated on edge hardware.
Role in the framework: Confidence-signal source: conformal calibration for distributed decisions and escalation.

Task: Long-horizon robot manipulation without a predefined skill library.
Method: LLM high-level plan, vision-plus-motion-planning sequencing, online RL for local interaction.
Setup and data: MuJoCo; Sawyer and Panda arms; Meta-World, Robosuite, Kitchen, obstructed tasks; >25 tasks up to 10 stages.
Key result: >85% success; RS-NutAssembly 96% ± 8% vs SayCan 23% ± 21% and TAMP 20% ± 30%; Kitchen 100% vs baselines 0%.
Limitation: Simulation only; requires pose estimation and motion planning; RL training per task.
Edge footprint (as published): RL training needs GPU and many simulator steps; LLM calls cloud-based. Deployment policy could be light.
Role in the framework: Baseline to beat / component to reuse: LLM-guided RL modality invocation.

Task: Improving general agent abilities of open LLMs without losing general capabilities.
Method: Instruction tuning on AgentInstruct trajectories mixed with general-domain instructions.
Setup and data: Llama 2 7B/13B/70B; held-in and held-out agent tasks and general benchmarks.
Key result: AgentLM-70B comparable to GPT-3.5-turbo on unseen agent tasks; general abilities maintained.
Limitation: Text-only agent tasks; teacher-generated data; full fine-tuning of large models.
Edge footprint (as published): Fine-tuning requires multi-GPU; 7B inference only marginal on Pi-class hardware even when quantised.
Role in the framework: Component to reuse: data-mixing recipe to avoid forgetting during orchestrator fine-tuning.

Task: Improving language agents from environment rewards via a learned retrospective model.
Method: Frozen actor LLM; separate retrospective LM fine-tuned with policy gradient to generate failure reflections and plans for prompt refinement.
Setup and data: Multiple environments and tasks (details not given in the abstract).
Key result: Agents improve over trials and outperform baselines not using environment gradients (no figures in the abstract).
Limitation: Requires repeated reward-bearing trials; improvement only via prompts; environments and numbers not verified here.
Edge footprint (as published): Retrospective model is small and trainable on a GPU; actor may be a cloud LLM. Retrospective component could in principle be edge-sized.
Role in the framework: Component to reuse / competing approach: small reward-trained module steering a frozen agent, analogous to LoRA-tuned orchestrator.

Task: RL fine-tuning of vision-language models for multi-step decision-making.
Method: PPO on a VLM generating chain-of-thought then an action; rewards from environment.
Setup and data: LLaVA-v1.6-Mistral-7B; gym_cards (NumberLine, EZPoints, Points24, Blackjack) and ALFWorld.
Key result: EZPoints 50.0% vs GPT-4V 10.5%; Blackjack 40.2% vs 25.5%; ALFWorld avg 21.7% vs 19.4%; CoT removal hurts.
Limitation: Low absolute ALFWorld success; RL compute heavy; text/game environments only.
Edge footprint (as published): 7B VLM RL training needs GPUs; inference of 7B VLM slow on Pi-class hardware.
Role in the framework: Competing approach / component: RL fine-tuning of the decision model with CoT.

Task: Learning transferable visual representations from natural-language supervision.
Method: Contrastive image–text pre-training; zero-shot classification via text prompts.
Setup and data: 400M web image–text pairs; evaluation on 30+ vision datasets.
Key result: Zero-shot ImageNet accuracy matching original ResNet-50 without its 1.28M training examples.
Limitation: Weak on fine-grained/abstract tasks; web-data biases; similarity scores not calibrated.
Edge footprint (as published): Pre-training needs large GPU clusters; small CLIP variants (ViT-B) run inference on a Pi 5 at low frame rates.
Role in the framework: Component to reuse / confidence-signal source: perception backbone with open-vocabulary similarity scores.

Task: Language-conditioned tabletop manipulation combining semantics and spatial precision.
Method: Two-stream imitation-learning architecture: CLIP semantic stream plus Transporter spatial stream.
Setup and data: Simulated (Ravens-based) and real-world tabletop tasks; 10 simulated and 9 real tasks.
Key result: Single multi-task policy on 10 sim + 9 real tasks better than or comparable to single-task policies.
Limitation: Planar pick-and-place primitives; top-down view; demonstration-dependent.
Edge footprint (as published): Moderate-size network; training on GPU; inference feasible on embedded GPU, slow on Pi CPU.
Role in the framework: Baseline to beat / confidence-signal source: imitation modality with affordance heatmaps.

Task: A single generalist agent across tasks, modalities and embodiments.
Method: Tokenise all modalities and actions; train one transformer with shared weights.
Setup and data: Atari, image captioning, dialogue, real-robot block stacking, among others.
Key result: One network performs diverse tasks including real-robot block stacking (no numbers in abstract).
Limitation: Specialist-level performance not reached on all tasks; large model; not open.
Edge footprint (as published): Reported model around 1.2B parameters (not stated in the abstract); too slow for real-time control on Pi CPU.
Role in the framework: Competing approach: monolithic generalist versus modality orchestration.

Task: Multi-task, language-conditioned 6-DoF manipulation from few demonstrations.
Method: Perceiver Transformer over voxelised RGB-D and language, predicting next best voxel action (behaviour cloning).
Setup and data: 18 RLBench tasks (249 variations) and 7 real-world tasks (18 variations).
Key result: Significantly outperforms image-to-action and 3D ConvNet baselines (no specific numbers in abstract).
Limitation: Requires calibrated RGB-D and motion planner; voxel grids memory-intensive.
Edge footprint (as published): Voxel transformer needs a GPU; not Pi-class. LeKiwi lacks depth sensing.
Role in the framework: Baseline to beat: imitation modality with strong 3D prior.

Task: Scalable real-world robot control from large, diverse demonstration data.
Method: Transformer tokenising images and language, outputting discretised actions; scaling study over data/model size and diversity.
Setup and data: Large-scale real-robot data collection with mobile manipulators performing real-world tasks.
Key result: Promising scaling properties with data size, model size and diversity (no numbers in abstract).
Limitation: Expensive data collection; imitation only; no uncertainty estimate.
Edge footprint (as published): Tens of millions of parameters but designed for onboard GPU at a few Hz; Pi CPU insufficient without optimisation.
Role in the framework: Evaluation reference / baseline: large-scale imitation policy.

Task: Transferring web-scale vision-language knowledge to robot control.
Method: Represent actions as text tokens; co-fine-tune large VLMs on robot and web vision-language data.
Setup and data: Real robot manipulation; 6,000 evaluation trials.
Key result: Improved generalisation to novel objects and emergent semantic reasoning (6,000 trials).
Limitation: Very large models; cloud inference; physical skills limited to robot data distribution.
Edge footprint (as published): Multi-billion-parameter VLMs served from cloud TPUs; far beyond Pi-class.
Role in the framework: Competing approach: end-to-end VLA versus modular orchestration.

Task: General robot manipulation specified via multimodal (text and image) prompts.
Method: Transformer agent encoding multimodal prompts and autoregressively decoding actions; imitation learning.
Setup and data: VIMA-Bench simulation: thousands of procedurally generated tabletop tasks, 600K+ expert trajectories, four-level generalisation protocol.
Key result: Up to 2.9× zero-shot success over alternatives; 2.7× better with 10× less data.
Limitation: Simulation only; high-level action primitives.
Edge footprint (as published): Model sizes range to a few hundred million parameters (not stated in the abstract); GPU inference; small variants possibly edge-feasible.
Role in the framework: Evaluation reference: prompt-conditioned imitation and generalisation protocol.

Task: Open-source generalist vision-language-action policy with efficient adaptation.
Method: 7B VLA: Llama 2 backbone with fused DINOv2 + SigLIP visual encoder; discretised action tokens; LoRA fine-tuning and quantisation.
Setup and data: 970k real-robot demonstrations (Open X-Embodiment); 29 tasks across multiple embodiments; fine-tuning evaluations.
Key result: +16.5% absolute success over RT-2-X (55B) with 7× fewer parameters; +20.4% over Diffusion Policy in multi-task fine-tuning.
Limitation: 7B parameters; low control frequency; single-image input; no uncertainty output.
Edge footprint (as published): 7B model needs GPU (quantised fits consumer GPU); not Pi 5-native — would require an offboard GPU.
Role in the framework: Baseline to beat / component to reuse: open VLA for imitation modality; evidence for LoRA adaptation of robot policies.

Task: Open-source generalist robot policy adaptable to new sensors and action spaces.
Method: Transformer policy with language or goal-image conditioning, trained on Open X-Embodiment; fine-tuning to new observations/actions.
Setup and data: 800k trajectories; experiments across 9 robotic platforms.
Key result: Effective fine-tuning to new observation/action spaces within a few hours on consumer GPUs (9 platforms).
Limitation: GPU needed for fine-tuning; zero-shot performance platform-dependent.
Edge footprint (as published): Smaller than 7B VLAs (tens of millions of parameters, not stated in the abstract); inference plausible on embedded GPU, marginal on Pi 5 CPU.
Role in the framework: Baseline to beat / component to reuse: open policy initialisation for imitation modality.

Task: Generalist dexterous robot control with a VLM-based flow-matching policy.
Method: Flow-matching action generation on a pre-trained VLM; large-scale multi-robot pre-training; fine-tuning for new skills.
Setup and data: Multiple dexterous platforms (single-arm, dual-arm, mobile manipulators); laundry folding, table cleaning, box assembly.
Key result: Zero-shot, language-following and fine-tuning capabilities demonstrated (no numbers in abstract).
Limitation: Large model; data largely proprietary; no explicit uncertainty output.
Edge footprint (as published): Billions of parameters; GPU inference required; not Pi-class (would need offboard compute).
Role in the framework: Baseline to beat / evaluation reference: state-of-the-art VLA with hierarchical high-level/low-level split.

Task: Self-improving multi-embodiment generalist agent for manipulation.
Method: Visual goal-conditioned decision transformer; few-shot fine-tuning; self-generated data fed back into training.
Setup and data: Simulated and three real robot embodiments; diverse manipulation tasks.
Key result: Adaptation to new tasks/robots with 100–1,000 examples; zero-shot generalisation reported.
Limitation: Heavy training compute; goal-image conditioning; not open.
Edge footprint (as published): Large transformer (Gato-based); datacentre training; not Pi-class.
Role in the framework: Component to reuse (conceptually): self-improvement via generated data and replay.

Task: Adapting open vision-language models to language-conditioned manipulation.
Method: OpenFlamingo backbone for per-step comprehension plus a policy head for history; imitation fine-tuning.
Setup and data: Language-conditioned manipulation benchmark (CALVIN per paper).
Key result: Exceeds state of the art by a large margin on the tested benchmark (no numbers in abstract).
Limitation: Mainly simulation; large VLM backbone; open-loop control trade-offs.
Edge footprint (as published): Billion-parameter-scale VLM backbone needs a GPU; the small policy head is light. Authors claim suitability for low-performance platforms.
Role in the framework: Component to reuse: frozen VLM + light policy head for imitation modality adaptation.

Task: Efficient VLA model with robotic reasoning and manipulation capability.
Method: Mamba state-space language model with vision encoder; alignment then fine-tuning of a small policy head (~0.1% of parameters).
Setup and data: Robotic reasoning benchmarks and manipulation in simulation and real world (details not verified).
Key result: About 3× faster inference than existing VLAs; policy head ~0.1% of parameters (other figures not verified).
Limitation: Still billions of parameters; benchmarks and real-robot extent to be confirmed from the full text.
Edge footprint (as published): 2.7B–3.2B-parameter backbone; GPU required; linear-time inference helps but still beyond Pi 5 real-time.
Role in the framework: Competing approach / component: efficient VLA with tiny adaptable head.

Task: Language-conditioned robotic manipulation with a compact VLA policy
Method: Small VLA on a compact pretrained VLM, trained on community datasets; asynchronous inference stack decoupling prediction from execution with chunked actions
Setup and data: Simulated and real-world robotic benchmarks; community-collected data from affordable platforms; LeRobot code base
Key result: Performance comparable to VLAs about 10x larger; trainable on one GPU, deployable on consumer GPUs or CPUs (abstract gives no further numbers)
Limitation: Abstract reports no parameter count, success rates or latency; CPU deployment performance unquantified in the abstract
Edge footprint (as published): Designed for single-GPU training and consumer-GPU/CPU inference; plausibly runnable on or near a Pi-5-class device with asynchronous chunking, but on-Pi latency needs verification
Role in the framework: Component to reuse (imitation/VLA policy native to LeRobot and SO-101); also baseline to beat

Task: Fast, data-efficient VLA-based robotic manipulation
Method: Compact VLA initialised from fast multimodal backbones plus a diffusion-policy action decoder added at fine-tuning; no robot-data pre-training stage
Setup and data: Simulation and real robots; comparison with OpenVLA; generalisation tests over instructions, objects, positions, appearance, background and environment
Key result: Faster and more data-efficient than OpenVLA with comparable or superior performance (no numbers in abstract)
Limitation: No quantitative figures in abstract; main comparison against one baseline
Edge footprint (as published): Designed for faster inference than 7B OpenVLA, but model sizes are unstated in the abstract; likely still needs a GPU for real-time control
Role in the framework: Competing approach / component to reuse (compact imitation policy; diffusion samples as fidelity signal)

Task: Efficient VLA inference for mobile manipulation on edge devices
Method: Non-autoregressive end-effector prediction plus small language model backbone within an OpenVLA-style architecture
Setup and data: Training comparison against OpenVLA; edge-oriented inference measurements (hardware not stated in abstract)
Key result: 7x inference speed-up from removing autoregression; comparable training characteristics to OpenVLA; improved memory efficiency
Limitation: Early results; no task success rates or real-robot closed-loop evaluation reported in abstract
Edge footprint (as published): Aimed at edge devices; exact device and latency unstated; SLM backbone still likely beyond a Pi 5 for real-time use without further compression
Role in the framework: Competing approach / design reference for edge-efficient imitation module

Task: Fine-tuning VLAs to new robots for speed and success
Method: Optimised Fine-Tuning recipe: parallel decoding, action chunking, continuous actions, L1 regression objective
Setup and data: OpenVLA base; LIBERO (four suites) in simulation; bimanual ALOHA real robot
Key result: LIBERO average 76.5% to 97.1%; 26x throughput; up to +15% absolute over π0, RDT-1B, Diffusion Policy, ACT on ALOHA
Limitation: Large 7B backbone; deterministic regression head provides no uncertainty estimate
Edge footprint (as published): GPU-bound (7B OpenVLA backbone); not runnable on a Raspberry Pi 5
Role in the framework: Baseline to beat / evaluation reference for VLA fine-tuning

Task: Action tokenisation for autoregressive VLA policies
Method: DCT-based compression tokeniser (FAST) and universal tokeniser FAST+
Setup and data: High-frequency dexterous robot data; FAST+ trained on 1M trajectories; scaled with π0 on 10k hours
Key result: Enables tasks where binning fails; matches diffusion VLAs with up to 5x less training time
Limitation: Inference cost of autoregressive decoding not quantified in abstract; large-scale training setting
Edge footprint (as published): Tokeniser itself is lightweight; the VLAs it serves need GPU training and inference
Role in the framework: Component to reuse (tokeniser; token likelihoods as confidence signal)

Task: Memory-efficient VLA for robotic manipulation on edge devices
Method: Native 1-bit (ternary) VLA on BitNet b1.58 2B4T; Quantize-then-Distill for the vision encoder
Setup and data: Simulation benchmarks and real-world tasks; baseline OpenVLA-OFT
Key result: Matches OpenVLA-OFT; 11.0x less memory; 4.4x lower end-to-end latency
Limitation: Work in progress; hardware and absolute latencies not stated in abstract; ternary kernels need specialised runtime support
Edge footprint (as published): Roughly 2B ternary parameters; memory footprint plausibly within Pi-5 RAM, but CPU latency on a Pi is unverified
Role in the framework: Component to reuse / competing approach for low-bit imitation module

Task: Cloud-free LLM-based robot planning via distilled on-device models
Method: PRISM: synthetic task/environment generation, teacher-LLM plan extraction, supervised distillation into a small student LLM
Setup and data: Three domains (mapping, manipulation, household); ground and aerial robots; indoor and outdoor environments; teacher GPT-4o, student Llama-3.2-3B
Key result: Student rises from 10–20% to over 93% of GPT-4o performance with synthetic data only; transfers across platforms
Limitation: Performance relative to teacher, not absolute; on-device latency and hardware not stated in abstract
Edge footprint (as published): 3B-parameter student designed for on-device use; likely needs an embedded GPU (e.g. Jetson-class) for interactive latency; a quantised 3B model on a Pi 5 would be slow
Role in the framework: Component to reuse (distillation pipeline for the orchestrator LLM) / competing approach

Task: Post-training quantisation of VLA models including DiT action heads
Method: Selective integer layout, attention temperature matching, output head balancing; calibration buffer only
Setup and data: Representative VLA models evaluated on LIBERO (simulation)
Key result: Task success above full-precision baselines; ~70% relative memory saving on quantised components
Limitation: Simulation only; bit-widths and latency not given in abstract
Edge footprint (as published): Reduces memory of GPU-scale VLAs; still unlikely to make them Pi-5-runnable alone, requires integer kernel support
Role in the framework: Component to reuse (compression of imitation module)

Task: Estimating model uncertainty in deep networks
Method: Dropout interpreted as approximate Bayesian inference in deep Gaussian processes; Monte Carlo dropout at test time
Setup and data: Regression and classification benchmarks, MNIST example; application to deep RL exploration
Key result: Considerable improvement in predictive log-likelihood and RMSE over prior methods (no numbers in abstract)
Limitation: Requires multiple stochastic passes; calibration sensitive to dropout rate; approximation quality debated
Edge footprint (as published): No training overhead; inference cost scales with number of samples (T passes), feasible on a Pi 5 for small networks at low T
Role in the framework: Confidence-signal source (epistemic uncertainty for perception and value estimates)

Task: Predictive uncertainty estimation in deep networks
Method: Deep ensembles with proper scoring rules and optional adversarial training
Setup and data: Classification and regression benchmarks; known vs unknown distribution test sets; ImageNet
Key result: Well-calibrated uncertainty, as good as or better than approximate Bayesian NNs; higher uncertainty on OOD examples (no numbers in abstract)
Limitation: Linear cost in ensemble size for training, memory and inference
Edge footprint (as published): Cost multiplies with M members; feasible on a Pi 5 only for small models or shared-backbone ensembles of heads
Role in the framework: Confidence-signal source (reference epistemic uncertainty)

Task: Modelling aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty for vision
Method: Bayesian deep learning framework combining heteroscedastic aleatoric outputs with MC-dropout epistemic uncertainty; learned attenuation loss
Setup and data: Per-pixel semantic segmentation and depth regression benchmarks
Key result: New state-of-the-art segmentation and depth-regression results at time of publication (no numbers in abstract)
Limitation: Epistemic estimate needs multiple forward passes; approximate posterior quality
Edge footprint (as published): Aleatoric head adds negligible cost; epistemic part multiplies inference by sample count, demanding on a Pi 5 for dense prediction
Role in the framework: Confidence-signal source (aleatoric/epistemic decomposition for perception)

Task: Confidence calibration of modern neural network classifiers
Method: Empirical analysis of miscalibration factors; comparison of post-hoc calibration methods; temperature scaling
Setup and data: State-of-the-art architectures on image and document classification datasets
Key result: Modern networks poorly calibrated; temperature scaling effective on most datasets (no numbers in abstract)
Limitation: Post-hoc, in-distribution calibration; no guarantees under dataset shift
Edge footprint (as published): Single scalar per model; negligible compute, trivially Pi-5-compatible
Role in the framework: Component to reuse (calibration of all confidence signals before fusion) / evaluation reference (ECE)

Task: Misclassification and out-of-distribution detection
Method: Maximum softmax probability as a detection score
Setup and data: Detection tasks in computer vision, NLP and automatic speech recognition
Key result: Baseline effective across all domains, but can be surpassed (no numbers in abstract)
Limitation: Inherits softmax over-confidence; weak on some far-OOD inputs
Edge footprint (as published): No overhead beyond a single forward pass; fully Pi-5-compatible
Role in the framework: Confidence-signal source (zero-cost baseline) / baseline to beat for uncertainty estimators

Task: Quantifying classification uncertainty in a single forward pass
Method: Evidential deep learning: Dirichlet over class probabilities, subjective-logic evidence, dedicated loss
Setup and data: Classification benchmarks with OOD and adversarial tests (datasets not named in abstract)
Key result: Reported strong OOD detection and adversarial robustness (no numbers in abstract)
Limitation: Preliminary theoretical analysis; faithfulness of epistemic interpretation later questioned; regulariser tuning
Edge footprint (as published): Single deterministic pass, negligible overhead; Pi-5-compatible
Role in the framework: Confidence-signal source (sampling-free perception uncertainty)

Task: Uncertainty estimation for regression in a single forward pass
Method: Evidential priors (Normal-Inverse-Gamma) over Gaussian likelihood; evidence regulariser
Setup and data: Various regression benchmarks including complex computer vision tasks; adversarial and OOD tests
Key result: Well-calibrated uncertainty; robustness to adversarial and OOD samples (no numbers in abstract)
Limitation: Epistemic estimate sensitive to regulariser; theoretical validity later debated
Edge footprint (as published): Single pass with four-parameter output head; negligible overhead, Pi-5-compatible
Role in the framework: Confidence-signal source (aleatoric and epistemic for continuous outputs)

Task: Embodied question answering with calibrated exploration stopping
Method: VLM-guided semantic map for exploration; conformal prediction on VLM answer confidence
Setup and data: New EQA dataset on HM3D in simulation; real-robot experiments
Key result: Improved performance and efficiency over uncalibrated and non-VLM baselines (no numbers in abstract)
Limitation: Depends on large VLM; conformal guarantees assume exchangeability
Edge footprint (as published): Large VLM inference likely requires GPU or cloud; conformal step itself is cheap
Role in the framework: Confidence-signal source (conformal calibration of foundation-model confidence) / evaluation reference

Task: Learning control from raw pixels with deep RL
Method: Deep Q-network with experience replay and target network
Setup and data: Atari 2600 games (Arcade Learning Environment), shared architecture and hyperparameters
Key result: Human-comparable play on many of 49 games (from standard knowledge; (not stated in the abstract)
Limitation: Discrete actions only; sample-inefficient; no uncertainty over values
Edge footprint (as published): Small convolutional network; inference Pi-5-feasible, training at Atari scale needs a GPU
Role in the framework: Baseline to beat / component to reuse (experience replay, target networks)

Task: Deep exploration in reinforcement learning
Method: Bootstrapped DQN: multi-head Q-network with bootstrapped data, per-episode head sampling (randomised value functions)
Setup and data: Complex stochastic MDPs; Arcade Learning Environment (Atari)
Key result: Substantially improved learning times and performance across most Atari games (no numbers in abstract)
Limitation: Discrete actions; heuristic posterior approximation
Edge footprint (as published): Shared torso plus K small heads; inference overhead modest and Pi-5-feasible for small networks
Role in the framework: Confidence-signal source (head disagreement as value uncertainty / policy variance for RL module)

Task: Stable, simple policy-gradient reinforcement learning
Method: Clipped surrogate objective enabling multiple minibatch epochs per batch
Setup and data: Simulated robotic locomotion and Atari benchmarks
Key result: Outperforms other online policy-gradient methods; favourable balance of sample complexity, simplicity and wall time (no numbers in abstract)
Limitation: On-policy; sample-inefficient for real robots
Edge footprint (as published): Small policy/value networks run on a Pi 5; training usually done in simulation on a workstation
Role in the framework: Baseline to beat / confidence-signal source (policy entropy/variance)

Task: Learning from sparse binary rewards in goal-conditioned RL
Method: Hindsight Experience Replay: goal relabelling in the replay buffer, combined with off-policy RL
Setup and data: Simulated robotic arm: pushing, sliding, pick-and-place with binary rewards; sim-to-real deployment on a physical robot
Key result: HER crucial for training success in ablations; simulated policies complete the task on a physical robot (no numbers in abstract)
Limitation: Requires goal-conditioned tasks with recomputable rewards; limited real-robot evaluation
Edge footprint (as published): Replay relabelling is cheap; off-policy training typically on a workstation GPU/CPU, not on a Pi 5
Role in the framework: Component to reuse (replay relabelling for online improvement of the RL module)

Task: Sample-efficient, stable model-free continuous control
Method: Soft actor-critic: off-policy maximum-entropy actor-critic with stochastic actor
Setup and data: Continuous-control benchmark tasks in simulation
Key result: State-of-the-art performance over prior on- and off-policy methods; stable across seeds (no numbers in abstract)
Limitation: Simulation-only evaluation in this paper; entropy temperature sensitivity
Edge footprint (as published): Small MLP actor and critics; inference Pi-5-feasible; on-board training possible but slow for image inputs
Role in the framework: Baseline to beat / component to reuse / confidence-signal source (policy variance, entropy)

Task: Reducing overestimation bias in actor-critic RL
Method: TD3: clipped double-Q with twin critics, target networks, delayed policy updates
Setup and data: OpenAI Gym continuous-control tasks
Key result: Outperforms state of the art in every environment tested (no numbers in abstract)
Limitation: Deterministic policy; simulation-only evaluation
Edge footprint (as published): Small networks; inference Pi-5-feasible
Role in the framework: Baseline to beat / confidence-signal source (twin-critic disagreement)

Task: Closed-loop vision-based robotic grasping via RL
Method: QT-Opt: scalable self-supervised off-policy Q-learning with continuous action optimisation
Setup and data: Real-world grasping; RGB over-the-shoulder camera; over 580k grasp attempts
Key result: 96% grasp success on unseen objects; Q-network over 1.2M parameters; emergent regrasping and pre-grasp manipulation
Limitation: Very large real-world data requirement; single task family
Edge footprint (as published): Q-network inference modest, but training infrastructure is large-scale distributed; not reproducible on one Pi-class robot
Role in the framework: Evaluation reference / competing approach (RL-only manipulation at scale)

Task: Exploration in sparse-reward deep RL
Method: Random network distillation bonus; flexible combination of intrinsic and extrinsic rewards
Setup and data: Hard-exploration Atari games, notably Montezuma's Revenge
Key result: State of the art on Montezuma's Revenge; better than average human without demonstrations; occasionally completes level 1
Limitation: Evaluated on Atari only; novelty is not task relevance
Edge footprint (as published): Two small networks; negligible overhead, Pi-5-feasible
Role in the framework: Confidence-signal source (novelty/OOD signal) / component to reuse

Task: Offline reinforcement learning from static datasets
Method: Conservative Q-learning: Q-value regulariser yielding a lower bound on policy value
Setup and data: Discrete and continuous control offline benchmarks
Key result: Often 2–5x higher final return than prior offline RL methods
Limitation: Conservatism can slow later online fine-tuning; regulariser weight tuning
Edge footprint (as published): Standard actor-critic networks; training off-board, inference Pi-5-feasible
Role in the framework: Component to reuse (offline pre-training from replay) / baseline

Task: General model-based RL across diverse domains
Method: DreamerV3: learned world model with imagination-based behaviour learning and robustness techniques; single configuration
Setup and data: Over 150 diverse tasks; Minecraft diamond collection
Key result: Outperforms specialised methods across over 150 tasks; first to collect diamonds in Minecraft from scratch without human data
Limitation: Simulation/game evaluation; heavy training compute
Edge footprint (as published): Training requires a GPU; policy inference possibly feasible on-board but world model is large
Role in the framework: Competing approach / confidence-signal source (world-model prediction error for fault detection)

Task: Online refinement of large offline imitation policies
Method: Model-agnostic residual RL policy on a frozen base imitation model with controlled exploration
Setup and data: Eight tasks on ManiSkill and Adroit; base models Behavior Transformer and Diffusion Policy
Key result: Improves offline-trained policies while preserving smooth motion; avoids erratic pure-RL behaviour (no numbers in abstract)
Limitation: Simulation only; requires reward and online interaction
Edge footprint (as published): Residual policy is small; base imitation model cost dominates; residual training likely off-board
Role in the framework: Competing approach / component to reuse (IL-to-RL hand-over; residual magnitude as fidelity signal)

Task: Precise multi-step assembly with BC plus RL
Method: ResiP: closed-loop residual RL policy on a frozen chunked BC model
Setup and data: Precise assembly tasks (details not in the abstract)
Key result: Improves reliability over chunked BC (no figures in the abstract)
Limitation: Evaluation details and numbers not available from abstract; needs reward design
Edge footprint (as published): Small residual network; RL training likely in simulation off-board
Role in the framework: Competing approach / component to reuse (IL-to-RL residual refinement)

Task: Sample-efficient real-world RL adaptation of diffusion BC policies
Method: DSRL: RL over the latent-noise input of a frozen diffusion policy; black-box access only
Setup and data: Simulated benchmarks, real-world robotic tasks, adaptation of pretrained generalist policies
Key result: Highly sample-efficient real-world policy improvement without modifying base weights (no numbers in abstract)
Limitation: Needs reward; bounded by base policy's expressivity; no figures in abstract
Edge footprint (as published): RL agent over noise space is small; base diffusion policy inference cost dominates; potentially suited to on-device learning
Role in the framework: Component to reuse (RL steering of imitation module) / competing approach

Task: Offline RL and online fine-tuning for arbitrary policy classes
Method: PA-RL: sample actions, global re-ranking by Q and local gradient optimisation, then supervised distillation into the policy
Setup and data: Diffusion and transformer policies of varying size; real-world fine-tuning of OpenVLA with Cal-QL
Key result: Up to 2x performance and sample-efficiency gains; OpenVLA real-world success 40% to 70% in 40 minutes
Limitation: Large-model fine-tuning GPU-heavy; multiple action samples per step raise compute
Edge footprint (as published): Sampling-and-ranking multiplies inference cost; 7B fine-tuning needs a GPU; small policies feasible on-board for inference
Role in the framework: Component to reuse (critic-based refinement across policy classes; Q-spread as confidence) / competing approach

Task: Reinforced fine-tuning of VLA models for contact-rich real-world manipulation
Method: ConRFT: offline BC plus Q-learning, then online consistency-policy fine-tuning with human interventions
Setup and data: Eight diverse real-world manipulation tasks
Key result: 96.3% average success within 45–90 min online; 144% improvement in success rate and 1.9x shorter episodes vs supervised methods
Limitation: Requires human intervention during online learning; VLA compute not stated
Edge footprint (as published): VLA fine-tuning needs a GPU; not runnable on a Pi 5
Role in the framework: Competing approach / evaluation reference (IL-to-RL with human-in-the-loop)

Task: Online RL improvement of pretrained autoregressive VLAs
Method: Trajectory-level RL as multi-turn conversation; VLM-based process reward model; scaling techniques
Setup and data: OpenVLA-7B; 40 LIBERO manipulation tasks (simulation)
Key result: +4.5% over strongest fine-tuned baseline; matches π0-FAST
Limitation: Simulation only; heavy GPU requirements
Edge footprint (as published): GPU cluster-scale training; not Pi-5-compatible
Role in the framework: Competing approach / confidence-signal source (process reward model as progress signal)

Task: Scaling RL training for VLA models
Method: SimpleVLA-RL on veRL: VLA trajectory sampling, parallelisation, multi-environment rendering, exploration strategies
Setup and data: OpenVLA-OFT base; LIBERO, RoboTwin 1.0 and 2.0; real-world tasks
Key result: SoTA on LIBERO; outperforms π0 on RoboTwin; surpasses SFT in real world (no numbers in abstract); 'pushcut' phenomenon
Limitation: GPU-intensive; numbers not in abstract
Edge footprint (as published): Large-scale GPU training; not Pi-5-compatible
Role in the framework: Evaluation reference / competing approach (upper bound for RL-refined VLA)

Task: Imitation learning under distribution shift
Method: DAgger: iterative dataset aggregation with expert relabelling; no-regret reduction
Setup and data: Two imitation learning problems and one sequence-labelling benchmark
Key result: Outperforms prior approaches (no numbers in abstract); theoretical guarantee under induced distribution
Limitation: Requires an interactive expert to label visited states
Edge footprint (as published): Algorithm-agnostic and lightweight; data aggregation feasible on-board, relabelling needs human or scripted expert
Role in the framework: Component to reuse (corrective relabelling for imitation/fault recovery) / baseline

Task: Imitation learning from expert demonstrations without reward or interactive expert.
Method: Adversarial occupancy-measure matching: discriminator provides surrogate reward for policy-gradient (TRPO-style) policy optimisation (GAIL).
Setup and data: Simulated high-dimensional control benchmarks (physics-based locomotion and control environments).
Key result: Significant gains over prior model-free imitation methods on complex high-dimensional environments (no figures stated in abstract).
Limitation: Needs many on-policy environment interactions; adversarial training can be unstable; simulation only.
Edge footprint (as published): Small MLP policy/discriminator cheap at inference, but training needs large numbers of simulator rollouts; training impractical on a Pi-class robot, inference feasible.
Role in the framework: Competing approach / imitation-modality component; discriminator output as a behavioural-fidelity signal.

Task: One-shot imitation of new task instances from a single demonstration.
Method: Meta-learning a demonstration-conditioned policy trained on pairs of demonstrations; soft attention over demonstration and context.
Setup and data: Simulated block-stacking task family with many task variants and instantiations (per abstract).
Key result: Qualitative claim of generalisation to unseen conditions and tasks via soft attention; no numbers in abstract.
Limitation: Simulation with state inputs; requires very large task family for training; generality largely anticipated rather than shown.
Edge footprint (as published): Moderate network size; inference plausibly feasible on CPU, but meta-training requires large-scale simulated data and GPU compute.
Role in the framework: Component to reuse / competing approach for fast imitation via meta-learning.

Task: Goal-conditioned visual manipulation learned from unlabelled play data.
Method: Play-LMP: self-supervised latent plan model (CVAE-style) over teleoperated play trajectories, goal-conditioned at test time.
Setup and data: Simulated robotic tabletop environment; 18 visual manipulation tasks; human teleoperated play.
Key result: Play covers ~4x more interaction space than demonstrations; Play-LMP substantially outperforms per-task expert policies on 18 tasks, more robust to perturbations.
Limitation: Simulation only; requires goal images at test time.
Edge footprint (as published): Moderate conv+RNN model; inference plausibly CPU-feasible, training requires GPU.
Role in the framework: Component to reuse (low-cost data collection for imitation modality); latent-plan likelihood as possible fidelity signal.

Task: Behavioural cloning for robot manipulation, including multimodal and discontinuous action mappings.
Method: Implicit BC: energy-based models trained with contrastive loss; actions inferred by derivative-free or gradient-based optimisation.
Setup and data: Simulated manipulation tasks, D4RL human-expert tasks, and real-robot contact-rich tasks from human demonstrations.
Key result: Often outperforms explicit MSE/MDN BC; competitive with or better than offline RL on D4RL human-expert tasks without rewards; real tasks with 1 mm precision.
Limitation: Iterative inference cost; EBM training can be sensitive to negative sampling.
Edge footprint (as published): Inference requires many energy evaluations per action; potentially heavy on a Pi CPU at control rate unless model is small.
Role in the framework: Baseline to beat / imitation component; energy values as action-confidence signal.

Task: Zero-shot generalisation of vision-based manipulation to unseen tasks.
Method: Interactive imitation learning from demonstrations and interventions; policy conditioned on language or human-video task embeddings.
Setup and data: Real robot data collection over more than 100 distinct manipulation tasks.
Key result: 24 unseen tasks performed with 44% average success without robot demonstrations for those tasks.
Limitation: Moderate success on unseen tasks; large-scale data collection effort.
Edge footprint (as published): ResNet-based policy with pretrained language/video encoders; inference feasible on modest GPU, borderline on Pi CPU.
Role in the framework: Baseline / evaluation reference for language-conditioned imitation; intervention mechanism relevant to handover decisions.

Task: Visuomotor imitation learning for robot manipulation.
Method: Conditional denoising diffusion over action sequences; receding-horizon control; visual conditioning; time-series diffusion transformer (and CNN variant).
Setup and data: 12 tasks from 4 manipulation benchmarks (simulated and real, per full paper); code and data released.
Key result: Consistent outperformance of prior state of the art, average improvement 46.9%.
Limitation: Iterative denoising increases inference latency; requires demonstration data per task.
Edge footprint (as published): Multi-step denoising is GPU-oriented; on a Pi 5 CPU latency is likely prohibitive without fewer steps, distillation or offloading.
Role in the framework: Baseline to beat / imitation component (LeRobot); sample dispersion as confidence signal.

Task: Fine-grained bimanual manipulation from demonstrations on low-cost hardware.
Method: Action Chunking with Transformers (ACT): CVAE-style transformer predicting action chunks, trained on teleoperated demonstrations.
Setup and data: Low-cost bimanual robot with teleoperation rig (ALOHA); six real-world fine manipulation tasks.
Key result: 80–90% success on six tasks with ten minutes of demonstrations.
Limitation: Single platform, few tasks; task-specific training.
Edge footprint (as published): Compact transformer policy; GPU-trained, inference plausibly near-real-time on edge hardware with modest optimisation (not reported in abstract).
Role in the framework: Baseline to beat / imitation component in LeRobot for SO-101-class arms.

Task: Uncertainty-aware deployment of pre-trained language-conditioned imitation policies under new conditions.
Method: Temperature-scaling calibration of action distributions; uncertainty-aware action selection by aggregating local information of candidate actions.
Setup and data: Simulation; PerAct and RVT on RLBench, CLIPort on Ravens; distractor conditions.
Key result: PerAct 0.382→0.414, RVT 0.602→0.623, CLIPort mean reward 0.803→0.833; stack-blocks with distractors 79.63%→97.11%; assembling kits 48.32%→55.44%.
Limitation: Simulation only; modest nominal gains; requires discretised/heatmap-style action outputs.
Edge footprint (as published): Calibration adds negligible cost (single temperature parameter); base policies (PerAct/RVT) are GPU-bound transformers, not Pi-feasible as evaluated.
Role in the framework: Confidence-signal source (calibrated action distribution) / component to reuse for imitation modality.

Task: Damage recovery through self-modelling on a legged robot.
Method: Continuous self-modelling: candidate model generation, action selection to maximise disagreement between models, behaviour synthesis from best model.
Setup and data: Physical legged robot with induced limb damage (standard account).
Key result: Robot inferred its morphology and generated compensatory locomotion after damage (no figures reported here).
Limitation: Single robot and narrow damage set; computationally expensive model search.
Edge footprint (as published): Model search and behaviour synthesis were run off-board in simulation; not suited to real-time Pi-class execution without simplification.
Role in the framework: Competing approach / conceptual precursor for fault-adaptation modality; model disagreement as uncertainty signal.

Task: Rapid damage recovery for legged robots and manipulators without diagnosis.
Method: Intelligent Trial and Error: MAP-Elites behaviour-performance map built in simulation, then map-based Bayesian optimisation (GP) on the damaged robot.
Setup and data: Physical hexapod robot with multiple damage conditions; robotic arm experiment (standard account).
Key result: Compensatory behaviours found within a small number of trials and short time (exact figures not verified).
Limitation: Relies on a simulator and hand-designed behaviour descriptors; static damage conditions.
Edge footprint (as published): Map is precomputed offline (heavy, cluster-scale); online GP-based BO over a precomputed map is lightweight and Pi-feasible.
Role in the framework: Component to reuse / baseline for fault-adaptation modality; GP variance as confidence signal.

Task: Sim-to-real transfer of object localisation for grasping.
Method: Domain randomisation of rendering (textures, lighting, camera) in simulation; CNN detector trained purely on synthetic images.
Setup and data: Simulated training images; real robot grasping in cluttered scenes.
Key result: Real-world localisation accuracy 1.5 cm, robust to distractors and partial occlusion; successful grasping in clutter.
Limitation: Localisation only; randomisation ranges hand-designed.
Edge footprint (as published): Trained offline on GPU; resulting CNN detector modest in size and plausibly deployable on Pi-class CPU at low frame rates.
Role in the framework: Component to reuse (sim-to-real for perception/recovery modules).

Task: Online adaptation of continuous control to perturbations, damage and new terrain.
Method: Meta-learned dynamics-model prior (gradient-based and recurrent variants) adapted from recent data; model-based planning (MPC).
Setup and data: Simulated continuous-control agents; real dynamic legged millirobot with missing leg, slopes, terrains, payloads and miscalibration.
Key result: Rapid online adaptation demonstrated qualitatively in simulation and on the real millirobot (no numbers in abstract).
Limitation: Single small real robot; model-based planning cost; no quantitative figures in abstract.
Edge footprint (as published): Small dynamics network with sampling-based MPC; adaptation step lightweight, planning cost moderate; plausibly Pi-feasible at low control rates.
Role in the framework: Component to reuse / baseline for fault-adaptation modality; model prediction error as fault-trigger signal.

Task: Real-time online adaptation of quadruped locomotion to terrain, payload and wear.
Method: Base policy conditioned on extrinsics plus adaptation module estimating extrinsics from state-action history; trained entirely in simulation.
Setup and data: Simulation with varied terrain generator; zero-shot deployment on Unitree A1 over diverse outdoor and indoor terrains.
Key result: Adaptation in fractions of a second; state-of-the-art performance in real and simulated experiments (no numbers in abstract).
Limitation: Locomotion only; adaptation bounded by simulated variation range.
Edge footprint (as published): Small MLP/1-D CNN networks run onboard at control rate; clearly Pi-class feasible at inference; training requires GPU simulation.
Role in the framework: Component to reuse (fault-adaptation modality); extrinsics estimate as fault signal.

Task: Robot failure explanation and correction via LLM reasoning.
Method: Hierarchical summarisation of multisensory robot experience; LLM failure reasoning; language-based correction planner.
Setup and data: RoboFail dataset of tasks and failure scenarios (simulation and real robot per paper); multisensory observations.
Key result: Informative failure explanations that assist successful correction planning (no numbers in abstract).
Limitation: Post-hoc analysis; relies on large LLM and perception-to-text quality.
Edge footprint (as published): Uses large (cloud) LLM for reasoning; perception summarisation also heavy. Not Pi-feasible as published; would require a small local LLM.
Role in the framework: Competing approach / component to reuse for LLM-mediated recovery; evaluation reference (RoboFail).

Task: Runtime failure detection for generative imitation policies.
Method: Sentinel: statistical temporal action-consistency detector for erratic failures plus VLM-based task-progress monitor.
Setup and data: Diffusion policies on mobile manipulation domains in simulation and on a real robot.
Key result: Detects 18% more failures than either detector alone; significantly outperforms baselines.
Limitation: VLM component is computationally heavy; limited set of domains.
Edge footprint (as published): Consistency detector negligible cost (Pi-feasible); VLM monitor needs GPU or cloud unless replaced with a small local model.
Role in the framework: Confidence-signal source (action consistency) / baseline for runtime monitoring.

Task: Real-time anomaly detection and safe fallback selection using LLMs.
Method: Fast embedding-space anomaly classifier triggering slow generative-LLM fallback reasoning, embedded in MPC with feasible fallback branches.
Setup and data: Dynamic robotic systems such as quadrotors and autonomous vehicles (primarily simulation per paper).
Key result: Fast classifier outperforms autoregressive GPT reasoning even with small language models (no numbers in abstract).
Limitation: Evaluated on vehicles rather than manipulation; slow stage still needs a capable LLM.
Edge footprint (as published): Embedding-based detector with small LMs is plausibly edge-feasible; generative fallback reasoning likely needs GPU or cloud.
Role in the framework: Competing approach / design pattern for budgeted two-tier orchestration; anomaly score as confidence signal.

Task: Improving long-horizon dexterous manipulation from natural-language corrections.
Method: Hierarchical policy: high-level language-skill selector over language-conditioned low-level skills; real-time language corrections and iterative retraining.
Setup and data: Real bimanual hardware, long-horizon dexterous tasks (details in paper).
Key result: Significant performance improvement without extra teleoperation (no numbers in abstract).
Limitation: Requires a human observer; skill library must be rich enough to express corrections.
Edge footprint (as published): High- and low-level policies are GPU-trained transformers; inference footprint not stated in abstract.
Role in the framework: Competing approach / component to reuse for online improvement of a high-level selector.

Task: Failure detection and explanation in robotic manipulation.
Method: Fine-tuned open-source VLM (AHA) trained on procedurally generated failure trajectories (FailGen / AHA dataset).
Setup and data: Simulated failure data for training; evaluation on real-world failure datasets, multiple robots and unseen tasks; integration into three LLM/VLM manipulation frameworks.
Key result: +10.3% over GPT-4o ICL; +35.3% over average of six models; +21.4% average task success in downstream frameworks vs GPT-4 models.
Limitation: VLM inference cost; synthetic failures may not cover all real failure modes.
Edge footprint (as published): Multi-billion-parameter VLM; requires GPU, not Pi-feasible without heavy distillation or offloading.
Role in the framework: Confidence-signal source / baseline for failure detection; data-generation method to reuse.

Task: Failure analysis and correction for VLA-based manipulation.
Method: Failure-centric dataset construction plus lightweight multimodal model for task understanding, failure analysis and correction; used as external supervisor.
Setup and data: 9,440 failure trajectories, 78,623 QA pairs, 53 scenes (sim and real); real-world VLA pipeline on four tasks.
Key result: +34.1% failure-analysis accuracy vs GPT-4o; 29.1% relative improvement across four real tasks; lower latency than GPT-4o.
Limitation: Only four real-world tasks; model still a multimodal network of unspecified size in the abstract.
Edge footprint (as published): Described as lightweight and locally deployable; exact size/latency not in abstract, likely needs a GPU rather than a Pi 5.
Role in the framework: Baseline to beat / component to reuse (local failure supervisor for recovery modality).

Task: Runtime failure prediction for generative (diffusion/flow) imitation policies without failure data.
Method: FIPER: RND-based OOD score in policy embedding space plus action-chunk entropy; conformal calibration on successful rollouts; windowed joint alarm.
Setup and data: Five simulation and real-world environments with diverse failure modes.
Key result: Better separation of failures from benign OOD and earlier, more accurate prediction than existing methods (no numbers in abstract).
Limitation: Requires representative successful calibration data; both indicators must fire.
Edge footprint (as published): RND network and entropy over sampled chunks add modest overhead to the policy; cost dominated by generating multiple action samples. Plausibly edge-feasible if the base policy is.
Role in the framework: Confidence-signal source (calibrated OOD and action uncertainty) / component to reuse for fusion.

Task: Runtime failure detection for imitation-learning manipulation policies without failure data.
Method: FAIL-Detect: scalar epistemic-uncertainty signals (learned, incl. flow-based density estimator, and post-hoc) plus conformal prediction thresholds.
Setup and data: Diverse robotic manipulation tasks with diffusion/flow policies (simulation and real per paper).
Key result: More accurate and faster detection than SOTA baselines; learned signals, particularly flow-based density, mostly consistently effective.
Limitation: OOD not equivalent to failure; relies on representative successful data.
Edge footprint (as published): Scalar signal networks are small; overhead modest relative to policy. Plausibly Pi-feasible if the base policy is.
Role in the framework: Confidence-signal source / component to reuse (conformal calibration of switching thresholds).

Task: Multitask failure detection for generalist VLA policies on unseen tasks.
Method: SAFE: lightweight detector on VLA internal features predicting a failure-likelihood scalar; conformal prediction for thresholds.
Setup and data: OpenVLA, π0 and π0-FAST in simulated and real-world environments; evaluation on unseen tasks.
Key result: State-of-the-art failure detection; best accuracy vs detection-time trade-off (no numbers in abstract).
Limitation: Needs failed rollouts for training; requires access to policy internals.
Edge footprint (as published): Detector itself is lightweight, but the host VLAs are multi-billion-parameter and GPU-bound; not Pi-feasible as evaluated.
Role in the framework: Confidence-signal source (policy-internal feature probe) / baseline for failure detection.

Task: Fast adaptation of RL agents to new tasks from a task distribution.
Method: RL²: RNN policy whose hidden state persists across episodes, trained by slow RL (policy gradient) to implement a fast RL algorithm in its activations.
Setup and data: Multi-armed bandits, tabular MDPs and vision-based navigation (standard account).
Key result: Learned agents adapt within few episodes; comparable to hand-designed algorithms on small problems (no numbers cited).
Limitation: Scaling to long horizons; dependence on task distribution design.
Edge footprint (as published): Recurrent policy inference is light (CPU-feasible); meta-training requires large-scale simulation.
Role in the framework: Competing approach / conceptual basis for in-context (weight-free) adaptation of the orchestrator.

Task: Learning optimisation algorithms.
Method: Coordinate-wise LSTM optimiser trained by gradient descent to minimise optimisee loss (learning to learn).
Setup and data: Convex quadratic problems, neural-network training (e.g. MNIST, CIFAR per paper), neural-art style transfer.
Key result: Outperforms hand-designed optimisers on trained task families and generalises to similar tasks (no numbers in abstract).
Limitation: Limited generalisation outside trained problem distribution; meta-training cost.
Edge footprint (as published): Small LSTM per parameter coordinate adds memory/compute overhead over SGD/Adam; feasible for small adapters on edge, costly for large models.
Role in the framework: Component to reuse (meta-learned optimisation for online fine-tuning); background.

Task: Few-shot adaptation across classification, regression and RL.
Method: MAML: optimise initial parameters so few inner-loop gradient steps generalise; second-order meta-gradient (first-order approximation possible).
Setup and data: Few-shot image classification benchmarks (two), sinusoid-style regression, simulated policy-gradient RL tasks.
Key result: State of the art on two few-shot classification benchmarks; good few-shot regression; faster RL fine-tuning (no numbers in abstract).
Limitation: Second-order cost and memory; hyperparameter sensitivity; assumes shared task structure.
Edge footprint (as published): Meta-training is GPU-heavy; test-time adaptation needs only a few gradient steps and is feasible on-device for small models or adapters.
Role in the framework: Component to reuse (meta-learned initialisation for on-device adaptation of orchestrator/adapters).

Task: Few-shot and zero-shot classification.
Method: Metric learning with class prototypes (mean embeddings) and distance-based softmax, trained episodically.
Setup and data: Few-shot image classification benchmarks (per paper); zero-shot on CU-Birds.
Key result: Excellent few-shot results; state of the art zero-shot on CU-Birds (no numbers in abstract).
Limitation: Unimodal class assumption; relies on quality of learned embedding.
Edge footprint (as published): Inference is one embedding pass plus distance computation; adding classes requires no gradient steps. Highly Pi-feasible with a small backbone.
Role in the framework: Component to reuse (on-device few-shot perception); prototype distance as confidence signal.

Task: Meta-learning parameter initialisations for fast adaptation.
Method: First-order meta-learning: FOMAML and Reptile (move initialisation towards task-trained weights); theoretical analysis.
Setup and data: Established few-shot classification benchmarks (per paper).
Key result: First-order algorithms perform well on few-shot classification benchmarks (no numbers in abstract).
Limitation: Evaluated on supervised benchmarks; RL and robotics not covered.
Edge footprint (as published): No second-order gradients, memory similar to standard training; meta-training still off-board, but inner loops are cheap enough for on-device use with small models.
Role in the framework: Component to reuse (low-cost meta-learning for orchestrator/adapter initialisation).

Task: Benchmark for meta-RL and multi-task RL in manipulation.
Method: Open-source suite of 50 simulated manipulation tasks with parametric variations; evaluation protocols for meta- and multi-task learning.
Setup and data: MuJoCo-based simulated Sawyer arm (per paper); 7 algorithms evaluated.
Key result: Single tasks learnable, but algorithms struggle with multiple tasks even with as few as ten training tasks.
Limitation: Simulation only; single arm embodiment.
Edge footprint (as published): Benchmark requires simulation on desktop/GPU; not intended for on-robot use.
Role in the framework: Evaluation reference (simulation testbed for meta-learning/RL modalities).

Task: Sample-efficient meta-RL with task-uncertainty reasoning.
Method: PEARL: probabilistic context encoder inferring latent task variables; off-policy actor-critic conditioned on latents; posterior sampling for exploration.
Setup and data: Simulated continuous-control meta-RL benchmarks (MuJoCo per paper).
Key result: 20–100x better sample efficiency and higher asymptotic performance than prior meta-RL algorithms.
Limitation: Simulation only; assumes test tasks lie within meta-training distribution.
Edge footprint (as published): Small MLP encoder and policy; inference Pi-feasible; meta-training requires substantial off-board compute.
Role in the framework: Component to reuse / confidence-signal source (task-posterior variance) for the RL modality.

Task: Approximately Bayes-optimal exploration in meta-RL.
Method: variBAD: recurrent VAE inferring posterior over latent task; policy conditioned on posterior; meta-trained.
Setup and data: Grid-world domain; MuJoCo meta-RL benchmarks.
Key result: Structured uncertainty-driven exploration in grid-world; higher online return than existing methods on MuJoCo (no numbers in abstract).
Limitation: Approximate inference; simulation only; requires known task distribution.
Edge footprint (as published): Small recurrent encoder and MLP policy; inference Pi-feasible, meta-training off-board.
Role in the framework: Competing approach / conceptual template for uncertainty-conditioned decision making by the orchestrator.

Task: Continual adaptation of a pretrained robot policy to a sequence of new tasks.
Method: Online Meta-Learned Adapters (OMLA): adapters trained with a meta-learning objective to transfer knowledge across sequential tasks; compared with LoRA.
Setup and data: LIBERO (OBJECT, SPATIAL, GOAL) in simulation; real Kinova arm pick-up tasks with 5–20 demonstrations.
Key result: Forward transfer 0.86 vs 0.71 (OBJECT), 0.69 vs 0.57 (SPATIAL), 0.58 vs 0.52 (GOAL) vs LoRA; real robot 84.0% vs 60.0% (20 demos), 48.0% vs 34.0% (10 demos).
Limitation: Single real arm, simple tasks; computational overhead of meta-objective unclear.
Edge footprint (as published): Adapter-based, so parameter and memory footprint is small; base policy and meta-updates likely GPU-trained. On-device feasibility on Pi 5 not demonstrated.
Role in the framework: Baseline to beat / component to reuse (meta-learned LoRA-style adaptation).

Task: Training shared models from decentralised, privacy-sensitive on-device data.
Method: Federated learning via FederatedAveraging: local multi-epoch SGD on clients, weighted model averaging at server.
Setup and data: Five model architectures, four datasets, including non-IID and unbalanced partitions (e.g. image and language modelling tasks).
Key result: Robust to non-IID and unbalanced data; 10–100x fewer communication rounds than synchronised SGD.
Limitation: Empirical; no formal privacy guarantees from averaging; requires a coordinating server.
Edge footprint (as published): Designed for mobile devices; local training of small models is feasible on Pi-class hardware, communication-bound rather than compute-bound.
Role in the framework: Component to reuse (multi-robot, data-local sharing of adapter/orchestrator updates).

Task: Automatic weighting of multiple regression and classification losses in multi-task scene understanding.
Method: Learnt per-task homoscedastic uncertainty used to scale each loss in a joint objective.
Setup and data: Single monocular-image network predicting per-pixel depth, semantic and instance segmentation.
Key result: Learnt weighting outperforms separately trained single-task models (abstract; no figures in the abstract).
Limitation: Task-level (not per-input) uncertainty; no epistemic component; vision benchmark only.
Edge footprint (as published): Training-time loss weighting adds negligible compute; the dense multi-task network itself would need a GPU for training, inference of a small variant could fit a Pi-class device.
Role in the framework: Component to reuse: uncertainty-based weighting of heterogeneous objectives or confidence signals in the orchestrator.

Task: Federated optimisation under systems and statistical heterogeneity.
Method: FedProx: proximal term on local objectives, variable local work; convergence analysis.
Setup and data: Realistic federated benchmark datasets (supervised).
Key result: +22% average absolute test accuracy over FedAvg in highly heterogeneous settings.
Limitation: Supervised setting only; requires a coordinating server.
Edge footprint (as published): Client-side cost equals local SGD plus a proximal term; feasible on Pi-class clients for small models, but requires a server for aggregation.
Role in the framework: Competing approach / optional extension: multi-robot adapter sharing; outside the core cloud-free design.

Task: Multi-view classification with per-sample trust estimation.
Method: Per-view Dirichlet evidence combined via Dempster–Shafer rule (evidential deep learning).
Setup and data: Multi-view classification benchmarks (details not given in the abstract).
Key result: Improved accuracy, reliability and robustness reported qualitatively in abstract.
Limitation: Static classification; independence assumption across views.
Edge footprint (as published): Fusion rule is closed-form and cheap; per-view encoders dominate cost; plausible on a Pi-class CPU with small encoders.
Role in the framework: Component to reuse / baseline to beat: evidential fusion of multiple confidence signals.

Task: Reliable multi-view classification under noise, corruption and OOD data.
Method: Variational Dirichlet evidence per view fused by Dempster–Shafer combination; theoretical analysis.
Setup and data: Multi-view classification benchmarks (details not given in the abstract).
Key result: Improved accuracy, robustness and trustworthiness claimed; no figures in the abstract.
Limitation: Static classification; evidence-independence assumption.
